name: Hinduism
texts: Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Ramayana, Mahabharata
summary: One of the oldest living religions, with ideas of dharma, karma and moksha.

name: Buddhism
summary: Teaches the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.

name: Jainism
summary: Strict non-violence (ahimsa) toward all life.

name: Sikhism
summary: Equality, honest work and service (seva).

name: Zoroastrianism
summary: An ancient faith of good vs evil; Parsis fled to Gujarat.

name: Judaism
summary: The oldest Abrahamic religion.

name: Christianity
summary: The largest religion; reached Kerala by tradition with St Thomas (52 CE).

name: Islam
summary: The second-largest religion.

name: Confucianism
summary: Ethics of family, duty and government.

name: Taoism
summary: Harmony with the Tao (the Way).

name: Shinto
summary: Worship of kami spirits.

name: Ancient Egyptian religion
summary: Gods like Ra, Osiris and Isis; afterlife judgment.

name: Greek religion and mythology
summary: Zeus and the Olympians.

name: Norse religion
summary: Odin, Thor and Ragnarök.

name: Stoicism
summary: Virtue and calm acceptance.

name: Bhakti movement
texts: Tamil hymns, later Kabir, Mira, Tulsidas
summary: Personal devotion over ritual and caste.

name: Sufism
summary: Dargahs of Ajmer and Nizamuddin; qawwali music.

name: Cuneiform
summary: The first writing, pressed with reed styluses.

name: Egyptian hieroglyphs
summary: Deciphered by Champollion in 1822.

name: Indus script
summary: Over 4,000 short inscriptions remain unread.

name: Oracle bone script
summary: Ancestor of Chinese characters.

name: Phoenician alphabet
summary: Ancestor of most alphabets.

name: Brahmi
followers: Evolved into most South and Southeast Asian scripts
summary: Deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

name: Kharosthi
summary: Written right to left.

name: Tamil-Brahmi
summary: Early Tamil writing.

name: Devanagari
summary: Evolved from Brahmi via Gupta script.

name: Greek alphabet
summary: First to write vowels.

name: Latin alphabet
summary: Used by ~70% of the world.

name: Arabic script
summary: Also used for Persian and Urdu.

name: Maya script
summary: A full logo-syllabic writing system.

name: Hangul
summary: Designed to be easy to learn.

name: Ol Chiki
summary: Script created for the Santali language.

name: Animism and shamanism
followers: Hundreds of millions follow indigenous religions
summary: Probably humanity's oldest religious outlook: the belief that animals, plants, rivers and mountains have spirits, with shamans entering trance to heal and to speak with spirits. Evidence includes Upper Palaeolithic cave art and burials with grave goods. It survives in many indigenous religions, from Siberia to the Amazon and India's Sarna faith.

name: Mesopotamian religion
summary: Each city had a patron god — Enlil at Nippur, Inanna at Uruk, Marduk at Babylon — housed in a ziggurat temple. Humans were believed to be created to serve the gods, and priests read omens in livers and stars, laying foundations for astronomy.

name: Vedic religion
summary: Worship centred on fire sacrifices (yajna) to gods such as Agni, Indra and Varuna, led by priests chanting Vedic hymns. Later the Upanishads turned inward to Brahman and Atman, and Vedic ritual evolved into classical Hinduism.

name: Ajivika
summary: A rival of Buddhism and Jainism that taught strict fate (niyati): all events are predetermined. Ashoka's grandson gave them the Barabar caves.

name: Charvaka (Lokayata)
summary: Ancient Indian materialism: only perception is valid knowledge, there is no afterlife or soul, and pleasure is the aim of life.

name: Manichaeism
summary: Mani taught a dualism of light and darkness, drawing on Zoroastrian, Christian and Buddhist ideas; it spread from Rome to China before persecution destroyed it.

name: Mahayana Buddhism
summary: The 'Great Vehicle' emphasised the bodhisattva ideal of saving all beings and spread to China, Korea, Japan and Tibet.

name: Shia and Sunni split
summary: Disagreement over who should lead Muslims after Muhammad — elected caliphs or Ali's family — divided Sunni and Shia Islam; Husain's death at Karbala (680) deepened it.

name: Protestantism
summary: Luther's Ninety-five Theses challenged indulgences and papal authority, launching the Reformation and new churches.

name: Bahá'í Faith
summary: Teaches the unity of God, religions and humanity.

name: Brahmo Samaj and Arya Samaj
summary: 19th-century Hindu reform movements against idol worship, caste and child marriage.

name: Neo-Buddhism (Navayana)
summary: Ambedkar converted with about 500,000 followers to reject caste.
